explicit_callers.ordering: after bounded staged writes; before optional close/cleanup
explicit_callers.return_handling: nonzero 16-bit result marks the enclosing operation failed

explicit_callers.ordering: after final staged writes; before temporary-state cleanup and diagnostics
explicit_callers.return_handling: direct result is not consumed by the immediately following instructions

conditional_caller_groups.behavior: Flushes dirty file objects at page-copy, cache-transition, and transfer-finalization boundaries. Several callers independently test a 16-bit pending-write state before invoking the wrapper.
Independently flushes up to three owned file objects before detaching linked cache records.
Flushes after successful metadata/index writes, both when updating an existing extent and when creating a new extent.

durability_conclusions: The engine has no universal write-through rule: ordinary successful writes may remain pending behind the file-object dirty state.
Explicit synchronous flushing is concentrated at recovery/log serialization finalization and selected cache, teardown, and metadata consistency boundaries.
Grouped teardown does not rely solely on the wrapper's flag gate; it first checks a separate per-object pending counter for each of three owned file objects.
No direct caller of either wrapper proves the complete BTRVLOG.TRN record format or the full crash-replay algorithm.
bounded_unknowns: Semantic names of the recovery/log records written by the two explicit-flush callers
Whether every transaction-end path reaches one of these direct callers or uses an indirect/dynamic path
Exact background-cache cadence for dirty objects not crossing a proven flush boundary
Complete rollback and preimage replay ordering
